Configured MCP servers:
- fs: 1 tools, 1 resources, auth=bearerToken
- browser: 0 tools, 0 resources, auth=notLoggedIn

availableCommands.name: plan
availableCommands.description: Turn plan mode on.

availableCommands.name: mcp
availableCommands.description: List configured Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools.

availableCommands.name: skills
availableCommands.description: List available skills.

availableCommands.name: status
availableCommands.description: Display session configuration and token usage.

availableCommands.name: review
availableCommands.description: Review uncommitted changes, or review with custom instructions.

availableCommands.name: review-branch
availableCommands.description: Review changes relative to a base branch.

availableCommands.name: review-commit
availableCommands.description: Review a specific commit.

availableCommands.name: compact
availableCommands.description: Summarize conversation to avoid hitting the context limit.

availableCommands.name: goal
availableCommands.description: Set a goal to keep pursuing.

availableCommands.name: logout
availableCommands.description: Sign out of Codex. This option is available when you are logged in via ChatGPT.

availableCommands.name: ps
availableCommands.description: List background terminal processes.

availableCommands.name: $agenthub-cli
availableCommands.description: Manage AgentHub resources (skills, agents, prompts, steering, hooks, powers) from Ericsson's DevPortal catalog. Use when installing skills, searching the catalog, publishing resources, checking for updates, removing resources, or troubleshooting agenthub-cli. Trigger on install skill, add resource, search catalog, find skill, publish resource, update resources, list installed, remove skill, agenthub, agenthub-cli doctor. Exclude creating skills from scratch (use skill-creator), general package management.

availableCommands.name: $archify
availableCommands.description: Create professional architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow, and lifecycle/state diagrams as standalone HTML files with SVG graphics, a built-in dark/light theme toggle, and one-click export to PNG / JPEG / WebP / SVG. Accepts plain-language descriptions or pasted Mermaid code (flowchart, sequenceDiagram, stateDiagram) and lays the diagram out from scratch in archify style. Use when the user asks for system architecture diagrams, infrastructure diagrams, cloud architecture visualizations, security diagrams, network topology, technical workflows, approval flows, runbooks, CI/CD flows, process diagrams, API call sequences, request lifecycles, data pipelines, ETL/ELT maps, PII boundaries, data lineage, state machines, lifecycle diagrams, status transitions, or asks to convert/beautify a Mermaid diagram.

availableCommands.name: $codebase-memory-mcp
availableCommands.description: Index a repository into a persistent SQLite knowledge graph of functions, classes, call chains, HTTP routes, and cross-service links — then query it via the `codebase-memory-mcp cli` command for structural code intelligence with 120x fewer tokens than grep/file-reading. Use this skill whenever the user wants to index a codebase, search code structurally, trace call paths, run Cypher graph queries, get architecture summaries, find dead code, detect changes, manage ADRs, or perform any codebase exploration that benefits from a knowledge graph. Trigger on "index this project", "codebase memory", "search graph", "trace calls", "call graph", "impact analysis", "who calls", "find dead code", "code architecture", "cypher query", "graph query", "codebase-memory-mcp", "cbm". Also use proactively when the user asks complex structural questions about a codebase (e.g. "what functions call X", "what's the architecture of this project", "find unused functions") — the graph can answer these in a single query instead of dozens of file reads.

availableCommands.name: $codex-update-compat
availableCommands.description: Upgrade Codex in this repository and resolve compatibility regressions caused by app-server schema/protocol changes. Use when bumping Codex/npm package versions, regenerating `src/app-server` types, fixing TypeScript errors after update, repairing event mappings, and updating tests/snapshots to match new Codex behavior (especially model list, thread/session fields, sandbox policy shape, and tool/event notifications).

availableCommands.name: $commit-message
availableCommands.description: Generate conventional commit messages with gitemojis following Ericsson internal guidelines. Use when user wants to create a commit message, write commit messages, or needs help with git commit format. Triggers on "commit message", "write commit", "git commit".

availableCommands.name: $confluence-skill
availableCommands.description: Confluence workflows — pages, search, spaces, comments, and attachments via REST API. Use whenever the user works with Confluence in any way, even if they just say 'wiki' or mention a page title. Trigger on create page, update page, edit page, search confluence, find page, wiki page, CQL, confluence space, list spaces, add comment, inline comments, reply to comment, unresolved comments, upload attachment, download attachment, confluence, wiki, eteamspace, page labels, move page, child pages, page tree. Exclude Jira operations, SharePoint, DevPortal, TechDocs publishing.

availableCommands.name: $devportal-skill
availableCommands.description: Create, update, delete, search, and manage entities and relationships on Ericsson's DevPortal (Backstage catalog) via REST APIs. Use whenever the user wants to register a new component/API/system on DevPortal, update entity metadata or relationships (hasPart, partOf, dependsOn, consumesApis, etc.), delete catalog entries, set up catalog-info.yaml files, validate entities, bulk import, scaffold from self-service templates, search/discover catalog entities, or programmatically manage the DevPortal catalog. Also trigger when users mention "catalog-info API", "create entity", "register on devportal", "update devportal", "entity relationships", "hasPart", "partOf", "dependsOn", "catalog-info.yaml", "devportal CRUD", "link entities", "find component", "search devportal", "golden path", "scaffold template". Exclude agenthub-cli publish operations, DevPortal UI questions, Backstage plugin development.

availableCommands.name: $gerrit-skill
availableCommands.description: Gerrit Code Review API workflows — search changes, review code, post comments, set labels, push changes, manage reviewers, and submit merges. Use whenever the user works with Gerrit in any way. Trigger on gerrit review, gerrit change, push to gerrit, code review, submit change, gerrit comment, gerrit label, +1, +2, -1, -2, refs/for, cherry-pick gerrit, abandon change, gerrit dashboard, my open reviews, awaiting review, gerrit search, gerrit. Exclude GitLab MRs, GitHub PRs, Bitbucket.

availableCommands.name: $jira-skill
availableCommands.description: JIRA workflows — create issues, search with JQL, link issues, manage epics, format descriptions, and discover project fields via REST API (v10.3+). Use whenever the user works with JIRA in any way. Trigger on create issue, create story, create bug, create epic, new jira issue, search jira, JQL, link issues, epic link, convert issue type, jira formatting, update issue, jira comment, jira, eteamproject. Exclude Confluence operations, GitLab issues, sprint management.

availableCommands.name: $simplify
availableCommands.description: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found. Use when simplifying code, cleaning up recent changes, or improving code maintainability.

availableCommands.name: $skill-creator
availableCommands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.

availableCommands.name: $test-coverage-gap
availableCommands.description: Find untested code paths by cross-referencing module analysis docs (e.g. gupfd-module-analysis.md) against existing unit tests, then generate missing test code following established patterns. Use this skill whenever the user asks to "check missing tests", "find untested methods", "add test coverage", "check SFT flow coverage", "pinpoint missing tests", "add unit tests for uncovered code", or wants to compare documented data flows against actual test files. Also use proactively when the user mentions a module analysis document and wants to verify test coverage against it. Works with codebase-memory-mcp for call chain verification.

availableCommands.name: $vuln-nist
availableCommands.description: Query NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD) for CVE information, vulnerability searches, CPE-based lookups, CISA KEV catalog entries, and CVE change history using the local vuln-nist-mcp-server CLI runner. Use whenever the user asks about CVEs, vulnerabilities, NVD, security advisories, CISA KEV, CPE vulnerabilities, CVE history, or wants to look up a specific CVE ID. Trigger on CVE-*, vulnerability search, NVD lookup, security vulnerability, CISA KEV, known exploited, CPE vulnerabilities, CVE change history, recent vulnerabilities, buffer overflow CVE, remote code execution CVE, what vulnerabilities affect, is there a CVE for. Exclude Nessus scans, vulnerability scanning tools, penetration testing, CVSS score calculation.

availableCommands.name: $zhihu
availableCommands.description: 使用知乎开放平台搜索知乎和全网内容、获取热榜、调用知乎直答，或读取当前用户自己的知乎创作、关注与收藏。用户提到知乎搜索、社区观点、真实经验、热点、热榜、知乎直答、我的知乎内容、我的关注、我的收藏、开放平台、API、MCP、Access Secret，或要求查看、安装和配置知乎 Skill 时使用。深度研究优先返回搜索原始来源；本人数据只读取完成任务所需的最小范围。

availableCommands.name: $imagegen
availableCommands.description: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas.

availableCommands.name: $openai-docs
availableCommands.description: Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, and self-knowledge; OpenAI APIs and ChatGPT Work. 'You'/'this app' means Codex only.

availableCommands.name: $plugin-creator
availableCommands.description: Create and scaffold plugin directories for Codex with a required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, optional plugin folders/files, valid manifest defaults, and personal-marketplace entries by default. Use when Codex needs to create a new personal plugin, add optional plugin structure, generate or update marketplace entries for plugin ordering and availability metadata, or update an existing local plugin during development with the CLI-driven cachebuster and reinstall flow.

availableCommands.name: $review-agent
availableCommands.description: Perform a read-only, defect-first review of a specified code change and return every actionable finding. Use when another agent delegates review of uncommitted changes, a base-branch diff, a commit, or custom review instructions.

availableCommands.name: $skill-installer
availableCommands.description: Install curated skills from openai/skills or other repos
